reason: This text establishes and encourages hierarchical structures throughout the covenant narrative at Mount Sinai. Multiple levels of hierarchy are emphasized: (1) God's supreme authority ('For all the earth is mine'), (2) Moses as the sole divine intermediary between God and the people, explicitly stated when the people request 'You speak with us and we will listen, but let not God speak with us'), (3) the elders as representatives between Moses and the people, (4) Israel elevated hierarchically among all nations ('You will be a precious possession to me from all peoples'), and (5) the establishment of a 'kingdom of priests,' formalizing priestly hierarchy. The text repeatedly encourages acceptance of this hierarchical order through the people's covenant affirmation ('All that the LORD has spoken we will do'), and Moses mediates all divine communication downward through established leadership structures. The hierarchy is functional and divinely ordained rather than merely descriptive.
